description: From 1 July 2025 money laundering in the Notice includes proliferation financing, so the para 4.1 risk assessment covers PF risks (para 2.1 fn 1; para 4.1 fn 3).
Issued under section 16 of the FSMA 2022 (para 1.1). The earlier Notice 626, issued under the MAS Act 1970, was cancelled with effect from 1 April 2024.
Applies to all banks in Singapore as defined in section 2 of the Banking Act 1970 (para 1.1); it is not issued under the Banking Act.

Both Notices received the same 2025 amendments (PF in ML, beneficial ownership of legal arrangements, STR copy to MAS on request), in effect from 1 July 2025 (MAS Consultation Paper P004-2025, Annex B).
Issued under section 16 of the FSMA 2022; applies to finance companies licensed under section 6 of the Finance Companies Act 1967 (para 1.1).
Both Notices received the same 2025 amendments, in effect from 1 July 2025 (MAS Consultation Paper P004-2025, Annex B).
Issued under section 16 of the FSMA 2022 (para 1.1).
Applies to holders of a capital markets services licence under the SFA 2001 and certain exempt persons (para 1.1).
Both Notices received the same 2025 amendments, in effect from 1 July 2025 (MAS Consultation Paper P004-2025, Annex B).
Issued under section 16 of the FSMA 2022 (para 1.1).
Applies to direct life insurers licensed under section 11 of the Insurance Act 1966 (para 1.1).
PSN01, PSN02 and Notice 626 received the same 2025 amendments, in effect from 1 July 2025 (MAS Consultation Paper P004-2025, Annex B).
PSN01 and PSN02 are issued under section 16 of the FSMA 2022 (para 1.1 of each).
PSN01 applies to PSA licensees providing a specified payment service; PSN02 to PSA licensees providing a digital payment token service.
Both Notices require suspicious transaction reports to be submitted promptly to STRO.
Issued under section 84 of the Variable Capital Companies Act 2018 (para 1.1), not under the FSMA.
Both Notices received the same 2025 amendments, in effect from 1 July 2025 (MAS Consultation Paper P004-2025, Annex B).
Issued under section 16 of the FSMA 2022 (para 1.1).
Both Notices received the same 2025 amendments, in effect from 1 July 2025 (MAS Consultation Paper P004-2025, Annex B).
MAS grants or refuses the licence under section 138.

The PSA regulates digital payment token services in Singapore; Part 9 covers Singapore-based providers serving customers outside Singapore, and excludes businesses licensed or exempt under the PSA for a DPT service (s.137(5)).
Section 21A (in force 4 April 2024) empowers MAS to set DPT safeguarding requirements by regulation.
PF risks are part of the para 4.1 risk assessment, done on their own or within the ML/TF assessment (MAS response of 30 June 2025, para 2.2).
Because money laundering includes proliferation financing, the CDD, screening and STR duties apply to PF (para 2.1 fn 1).
The statutory duty to report is CDSA s.45 (and the TSOFA); tipping-off is CDSA s.57 and TSOFA s.10B (Notice para 14 and footnote 14).
Screening (paras 6.39-6.42) and enhanced CDD (para 8.8) take account of MAS's sanctions regulations and the TSOFA; the freezing duties come from those instruments, not from the Notice.
MAS's sanctions regulations are made under section 192 read with section 15(1)(b) of the FSMA 2022.

Third-party reliance under para 9 does not apply to outsourcing: an outsourced service provider performs CDD measures on the bank's behalf, under its policies and controls (Guidelines to MAS Notice 626, paras 9-1 to 9-3).
Released by the PDPC; voluntary, and does not amend the PDPA.
CDSA s.45 is the statutory duty to disclose knowledge or suspicion.
Disclosures under s.45 go to a Suspicious Transaction Reporting Officer; STRO is established by s.5.
CPIB investigates offences under the Act; prosecutions need the Public Prosecutor's consent (s.33).
Section 84 empowers MAS to issue AML/CFT directions to VCCs (MAS Notice VCC-N01).
ACRA administers the Variable Capital Companies Act 2018.
MOM is responsible for the Act; it is not yet in force (target end-2027).
ACRA and SGX RegCo jointly set the climate reporting timeline (joint announcement of 25 August 2025).
STRs go to STRO (para 14.2); records about a matter under investigation are kept as STRO requests (para 12.5).
MAS's 2017 penalties on Credit Suisse and UOB were for breaches of MAS Notice 626.
Every holder of a licence granted under section 138 must comply with MAS Notice FSM-N27 (para 1.1).
A licensee must comply with MAS Notice FSM-N30 on technology risk management and refer to the TRM Guidelines (Guidelines on Licensing for DTSPs, para 5.5).
CDD records hold personal data. PDPA s.4(6): Parts 3 to 6B do not affect obligations imposed by or under the law, and other written law prevails where inconsistent.
